lines.text: Many learners say: I will pass in your house tomorrow.
Better: I will stop by your house tomorrow.
For a short visit, we say stop by.
The first! I will stop by your house.

data.wrong: I will pass in your house tomorrow.
data.right: I will stop by your house tomorrow.
data.why: For a short visit, we say stop by.

options: I will stop by your house.

en.tip: In Portuguese we say “passar na sua casa”; in English, for a quick visit, use “stop by”.
en.caption: Watch out for this common mistake! Many people say “I will pass in your house tomorrow.” The right way is “I will stop by your house tomorrow.” In Portuguese we say “passar na sua casa”; in English, for a quick visit, use “stop by”. Listen to Ama and repeat! Practice more in the Lexkite app.
